title: 28 U.S.C. § 1335 — statutory interpleader
summary: Statutory interpleader is a specific federal jurisdictional route for competing claims to money or property. The readings distinguish its minimal-diversity, fund, service, venue, and injunction provisions from ordinary Rule 22 interpleader.

sections.Role in the course: Statutory interpleader is a specific federal jurisdictional route for competing claims to money or property. The readings distinguish its minimal-diversity, fund, service, venue, and injunction provisions from ordinary Rule 22 interpleader.
sections.What to examine: Check the statutory amount, diversity among claimants, required deposit or bond, and the relevant service and venue provisions. Potential unliquidated claims can qualify under Tashire, but the scope of protective relief remains limited.
